headline: An oracle could cut 68% of Haiku $ (65% Sonnet), but half of all $ is orientation after the agent has already found the right file, and pre-loading content is net-negative under the cumulative-context model; the only realistic double-digit cost lever is a learned output budget (~11% of Haiku $, 0 on Sonnet), so stacked with pre-emptive friction and the commit habit Haiku can plausibly reach ~15-19% while Sonnet stays under 5%, and the real sink is failure (48-72% of $).
metric_name: share of $ per held-out control session saved (cumulative-context re-pricing from measured usage); also calls/session

best_realistic_lever.name: learned per-tool output budget (Read<=1000 tok head-weighted, Bash<=2000)

held_out.ci: 90% bootstrap over sessions (arm comparisons: over tasks)

ranked_levers_haiku_v2.lever: output trimming / Read paging (learned budget, PostToolUse)
vcs habit (unprompted git commit in 98/98 prompts)

ranked_levers_haiku_v2.realistic_usd: unknown; tracks failure (+2.5 calls in failed sessions)
~0 on new tasks (memory recall@5 of needed files 0.32)

haiku_vs_sonnet: Sonnet has less friction (1.1 vs 3.0 calls on the same repos), fewer dead ends (1.0 vs 3.6), almost no commit ritual, and range reads (trimming realistic 0 vs 11%). Its waste is orientation (56% of $) and failure (72% of $). Oracle (a) is similar (65% vs 67%). The stronger the model, the less there is for a procedural reflex to remove.
vs_baseline: Current (U11 + learned reflexes, +1.0 Ŝ calls post-hoc, +2.11 pre-emptive) sits inside the env-friction class, ceiling 4.6 calls/session Haiku, 11% $; the adage arm measured -0.64 friction calls [-1.12,-0.18] = 1.2% of $. Pre-emptive delivery at ~2.3 calls is about half the ceiling, which is the realistic max for this class (~5% $). The learned output budget is new and adds ~11% of Haiku $ (at +2.8 calls); nothing here adds >5% on Sonnet.
hard_coded_parts: role instrument (measurement only): tool names Read/Grep/Glob/LS/Edit/Write/MultiEdit, normalize.py explore flag, TEST_RX, SETUP_RX, git prefix (anatomy.py)
setup-role calls counted as env friction
test-path regex to split final diff into src vs tests (graded-src oracle only)
Claude Code read-before-edit rule in the needed slice and pre-load simulation
thresholds: stoplist df>2% (stoplist itself learned), re-invocation char-3-gram cosine>=0.35, token regex, 3.08 chars/token (fitted)
harm models: 1 extra call per trimmed result that lost a used line; 40 tokens per pointer
trim budgets keyed by tool name (harness label); budgets and head split are learned on train
build_recommendation: (1) A learned output budget in PostToolUse updatedToolOutput for Read and Bash: per-tool (then per-repo) token budget and head/tail split learned from the train traces' hindsight line-usage vs re-fetch cost, with an elision marker giving the line range to page. Expected -11% $ [-13,-9] per Haiku session at +2.8 calls, ~0 on Sonnet; gate it by the model's measured read behaviour and A/B it live (the harm model is the weak link). (2) Finish the pre-emptive friction rewrite (~5% on Python repos with Haiku, ~0 on Node/Go). (3) Don't build content pre-loading, AGENTS.md-style dumps, trace-memory answers for new tasks, or doom-stopping: each is measured zero or negative. (4) Point research at pass rate: failure carries 48-72% of $, and +5 points is -7%/-10% $ per resolved task.
so_what: If shipped: Haiku ~-15 to -19% $/task (trim -11% [-13,-9] + friction ~-5% + commit habit ~-3%; not strictly additive), calls roughly -2 net, pass rate unchanged; Sonnet <-5%. Confidence it survives a live A/B: moderate for trimming, high for friction. The >=20% target is not reachable by cost reflexes on a strong model; it needs a pass-rate lever.
